situation: My dog Rufus died last Tuesday and the house is too quiet without his collar jingling in the hall.
poem:
The hall is wide and empty of his jingle,
and Rufus keeps his silence in the dark.
Grey light, an empty collar on the hook,
and the house too large by one small dog.

situation: The letter came today: I have been accepted to the marine biology program in Bergen.
poem:
A letter, and the cold blue north says yes,
Bergen with all its green rooms underwater.
You will go down and learn the salted dark,
and the sea will teach you its long name.

situation: My mother's biopsy results come back on Friday and I have cleaned the kitchen three times.
poem:
Friday is a stone you cannot put down,
and the kitchen shines like something frightened.
Your mother's name sits waiting in an envelope,
and the clock goes on, and on, and on.

situation: I have been waiting at the DMV in chair forty-two for two hours and my number still has not been called.
poem:
The hours lie down and will not rise,
and time goes yellow in a room of strangers.
Somewhere a voice is calling, and not for you,
O long grey afternoon without an end.

situation: My landlord kept my whole deposit for one scuff on the baseboard and will not answer his phone.
poem:
He keeps your money for a mark of dust,
and will not lift the ringing telephone.
Go down and file the papers; make him pay.
There is a red thing in you; it is right.

situation: The tornado passed two streets over and our oak tree is still standing.
poem:
The roaring went by two streets to the north,
and the oak still stands with all its hands.
The sky lets go. The air comes back green.
Nothing of ours is broken. Nothing at all.

situation: I burned the first pancake again, the way my grandmother always did, and the smoke alarm went off.
poem:
The first attempt is always given to the fire,
and we forgive it, being old and human.
Failure has a warm brown smell about it,
and the second time the day comes right.

situation: My daughter Maya took her first steps across the kitchen tile this morning, straight into the dog's water bowl.
poem:
Maya crosses the tile on her own two feet,
and ends up sitting in the water bowl.
The kitchen rings with her astonished laughing,
and the day is gold from wall to wall.

situation: I sold my father's blue Volvo yesterday and forgot to take the pine air freshener off the mirror.
poem:
The Volvo goes, and the pine goes with it,
turning on its string in someone else's car.
Blue paint, blue evening, and your father gone,
and the driveway wearing an empty rectangle.

situation: I have to give a toast at my brother's wedding on Saturday and I have rewritten it eleven times.
poem:
You have written it and written it again,
and still the words go crooked in your mouth.
The day comes anyway, bright and unafraid,
and love will carry what the language drops.

situation: It has rained for six days and I have reread the same page of my library book four times.
poem:
The days go grey and grey and grey again,
and nothing moves except the falling water.
The mind slides off whatever it is given,
and the hours pool and will not drain away.

situation: Someone keyed my car in the grocery store lot while I was inside buying milk.
poem:
A white line dug the length of your blue door,
while you stood buying milk beneath the lights.
Some hand did it and went off whistling,
and the hot thing rises in your throat.

situation: My flight from Denver landed twenty minutes before the blizzard closed the runway. I have never been so glad to see a jetway.
poem:
The runway closed its white mouth after you,
by twenty minutes, and the snow came down.
You were already warm, already through the gate,
and Denver disappeared behind the glass.

situation: I found a five dollar bill in my winter coat pocket along with a movie ticket from last February.
poem:
The past leaves small change in the dark,
and hands it back when you have long forgotten.
A little luck, unlooked for and unearned,
and the grey day goes suddenly bright.

situation: My best friend Priya moved to Auckland on Sunday and we finished the last of the chili in her freezer.
poem:
Priya is gone, and the chili bowl is empty,
and Auckland has her morning, and her voice.
The freezer hums a cold and hollow note,
and Sunday took her out across the water.

situation: After eleven months of looking, I start the new job at the bakery on Monday.
poem:
Eleven months, and Monday opens like an oven,
warm brown air and the smell of rising bread.
Your hands will have their work at last,
and the long grey waiting is burnt off.

situation: My son has not texted back in three days and his last message was just a period.
poem:
Three days, and the little period holds shut,
a door with nothing written on its face.
You watch the phone the way you watched him sleep,
and the quiet gets heavier every hour.

situation: I finally fixed the squeaking gate with a bit of olive oil because I could not find the WD-40.
poem:
The small broken thing is mended now,
and the house is easier by one complaint.
There is a quiet pleasure in such work,
and the day moves easier for being fixed.

situation: My coworker Dan presented my spreadsheet in the Tuesday meeting and never once said my name.
poem:
Dan says your numbers in his own warm voice,
and never once the syllables of your name.
The room applauds a man who did not work,
and you sit burning in the second row.

situation: The cat came back after four nights out, thin and loud, and slept twelve hours on my sweater.
poem:
What went out into the dark has come home,
and the long worry folds itself away.
Sleep now fills the house from wall to wall,
and nothing is missing that was missing.
